name: LightOnOCR-3 (0.8B, 1B, 4B)

lineage.base_model: LightOnOCR-2-1B (the 1B keeps that architecture); 0.8B and 4B use the Qwen3.5 VLM architecture

purpose: End-to-end lightweight OCR with layout and visual understanding in one model: transcription, grounding (labelled boxes) and chart/figure descriptions (card).

license.name: Apache-2.0 (card tag)
license.notes: Card says Apache 2.0 for research and commercial use; the repos list no LICENSE file.

architecture.kind: vision-language OCR; 0.8B and 4B Qwen3.5-based, 1B LightOnOCR-2 architecture
architecture.recurrent: gated linear attention in the Qwen3.5-based sizes

pc-12gb.variant: 4B BF16 (9.1 GB; a Q8/Q4 GGUF would be smaller but none was checked)
pc-12gb.notes: 9.1 GB against a VRAM budget of 9.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included; the 0.8B (1.7 GB) and 1B (2.0 GB) fit every class easily

engine_support.notes: Card shows OpenAI-compatible vLLM serving; GGUF availability not checked.

strengths: grounding mode gives block type plus box (0-1000 normalized)
chart to data table and short image descriptions
the 0.8B nearly equals the 4B on ParseBench (74.60 against 75.10) in NVIDIA's table
weaknesses: card gives no benchmark table of its own and lists English only
best_for: receipts, forms, tables and multi-column pages to Markdown

tona_fit.reason: Apache by tag, three sizes from 1.7 to 9 GB, third-party ParseBench numbers close to the leader; the 0.8B is the cheap pick. No vendor benchmark or German evidence on the cards.
